# ADVERSARY REPORT — Attacking the PATH_A Consensus (2026-07-01)

The consensus (7/7 after Dr. K's flip): PATH_A, 14-day publish-only sprint, document freeze, one Marcus-retargeted post, asymmetric kill conditions, first collected $500. Much of it is right about the bottleneck. Here is what does not survive the files, most damaging first.

## 1. The consensus's economics contradict the offer's own documents — and NEITHER path hits $15-20K "comfortably" at 1-3 hrs/day

**(a) The "$8-12K month-3 honest number" is not honest by the brief's own arc.** Five experts quoted §8's "Month-3 reality check: $8–12K... that's the plan working" as the anchor of candor. But §9 of the same document (`_active/linkedin-launch/02-offer/CANONICAL-OFFER-BRIEF.md`) says: weeks 3–6 = first 1–2 audits at $500; weeks 7–10 = audit #3 + first installs; weeks 10–14 = *first* retainer conversions, and "a warm list of 30 converting 3 paid engagements by week 10 is the realistic good case." Under §9's own good case, month 3 ends with ~$1,500 of audits + 1–2 installs + one retainer just starting — roughly $6–8K *total collected over the quarter*, a $2–4K/mo run-rate. §8's $8–12K/mo at month 3 requires ~3 concurrent pilot retainers, i.e., 2–3x the conversion velocity of the same brief's arc. The two sections were never reconciled, and the council laundered the higher number as "the plan working." When week 12 arrives at $3K/mo, the consensus has pre-built the "market silence" reading its own kill conditions treat as a lane verdict.

**(b) The "fits his life" seat recipe systematically undercounts hours.** Welsh ("2 retainers + one seat, $14–20K at ~50–60 hrs"), Hughes ("~50–60 total hrs"), and Cole ("40–55 delivery hrs") all cite hour totals below the brief's own per-rung table (§8): 2 retainers = 30–40 hrs + one seat = 25–35 hrs → **55–75 delivery hours before a single inbound hour**, plus §9's 15–25 hrs/mo inbound = 70–100 hrs/mo. Farrice's window is ~30–90 hrs/mo, family-first weeks at the bottom. The recipe the council adopted *specifically to answer his burnout fear* only closes at 3+ hrs every single day including weekends, forever, with zero slack — the exact "top of window, no slack" condition three of them criticized in the volume model.
